comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose segment net revenue drivers for FY2024, attributing growth primarily to AI-related demand. AMD attributes its Client segment 52% revenue increase to strong demand for Ryzen processors. Broadcom attributes its Semiconductor Solutions segment revenue increase to strong demand for AI networking products, although it is partially offset by lower demand in other areas. While AMD's growth was broad-based in its Client segment (implied by the lack of offset mentions in the specific summary), Broadcom explicitly notes offsets from broadband and server storage products, showing a more mixed product demand profile compared to AMD's reported Client strength.

Net revenue from our semiconductor solutions segment increased due to strong product demand for our networking products, primarily AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for our broadband and server storage products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Total Intel Products revenue was $48.9 billion in 2024, an increase of $1.3 billion from 2023, driven by growth in both Client Computing Group (CCG) and Data Center and AI (DCAI) segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel report revenue performance for their respective Client/Client Computing segments in FY2024, highlighting growth driven by shipment volume increases. AMD reports a 52% increase in Client net revenue driven by a 34% rise in unit shipments and a 13% increase in ASP. Similarly, Intel reports that its Client Computing Group (CCG) revenue increased $1.0 billion, with Notebook volume increasing 12% from 2023, although Intel notes that Notebook ASPs remained roughly flat compared to AMD's ASP growth. Intel also reports a decrease in Desktop volume (-5%) and revenue, whereas AMD’s summary focuses on the aggregate growth without disaggregating desktop declines.

sentences.text: Client net revenue of $7.1 billion in 2024 increased by 52%, compared to net revenue of $4.7 billion in 2023, primarily due to a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price driven by strong demand for AMD mobile and desktop Ryzen processors.

▪CCG revenue increased $1.0 billion from 2023. Notebook revenue was $19.1 billion in 2024, up $2.1 billion from 2023. Notebook volume increased 12% from 2023, as customer inventory levels improved compared to higher levels in 2023. Notebook ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Desktop revenue was $9.7 billion, down $516 million from 2023. Desktop volume decreased 5% from 2023, primarily due to lower demand compared to 2023. Desktop ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Other CCG revenue was $1.6 billion, down $530 million from 2023, primarily driven by the exit of legacy businesses.

comparisons.peer_summary: Total revenue for 2024 increased 62% compared to 2023, driven by a 60% increase in DRAM sales (due to mid-40% bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth) and a 72% increase in NAND sales (due to low-30% bit shipment growth and low-30% ASP growth).
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose revenue growth drivers for FY2024 linked to semiconductor volume and price increases. AMD’s Client segment net revenue increased 52%, driven by a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in ASP. Micron’s total revenue increased 62%, driven by a 60% increase in DRAM sales (mid-40% bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth) and a 72% increase in NAND sales (low-30% bit shipment growth and low-30% ASP growth). Both companies attribute growth to simultaneous increases in physical volume (shipments/bit shipments) and pricing power (ASP/ASP growth), though the specific components (processors vs. memory) and magnitude of growth differ.
